title: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
hook: The animal kingdom splits along one simple line: do you have a backbone or not? The vast majority of animals don't.
key_points: Vertebrates have an internal backbone (spine); invertebrates do not.
The great majority of animal species — about 95% — are invertebrates, like insects and worms.
Vertebrates fall into five main classes: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
A backbone is part of an internal skeleton that supports the body and protects the spinal cord.
content_html: For all its variety, the animal kingdom is often first cut in two by a single question: is there a backbone inside? Animals with one are vertebrates; animals without are invertebrates. It feels like a tidy 50-50 split, but it isn't — the backbone-less animals dominate.
extra_html: About 95% of all animal species are invertebrates: insects, spiders, worms, snails, jellyfish, and countless others, most of them small. Vertebrates are the minority, but they include the large, familiar animals and divide into five main classes — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals. Their defining backbone is part of an internal skeleton that supports the body and shields the delicate spinal cord running through it. Encyclopaedia Britannica's article on the vertebrate explains how the backbone defines this group and what sets its five classes apart from one another.

related.title: The Animal Kingdom
related.hook: Sponges, spiders, sharks, and squirrels look nothing alike — yet all are animals, sharing a few deep traits that set them apart from plants, fungi, and microbes.

related.title: How Species Are Named
related.hook: Every species on Earth gets a two-word Latin name — like Homo sapiens — under a tidy ranked system invented 250 years ago that scientists still use today.

flashcards.prompt: What single feature separates vertebrates from invertebrates?

choices.text: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not
Vertebrates live in water; invertebrates live on land
Vertebrates are warm-blooded; invertebrates are cold-blooded

flashcards.explanation_html: The dividing line is the backbone. Vertebrates have an internal spine; invertebrates, like insects, worms, and jellyfish, lack one.

flashcards.prompt: What are the five main classes of vertebrates?
flashcards.back_html: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals — the five major groups of animals that have a backbone.

flashcards.prompt: Which group makes up the great majority of animal species?
flashcards.explanation_html: Roughly 95% of animal species are invertebrates — insects alone account for an enormous share. Vertebrates are a small, though familiar, minority.
